1: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm centered on objects containing data (attributes) and code (methods). The four fundamental principles are: 1. Encapsulation - bundling data and methods while restricting direct access. 2. Abstraction - hiding internal implementation complexity. 3. Inheritance - creating new classes based on existing classes to reuse code. 4. Polymorphism - allowing entities to take on different forms depending on context.
2: Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common superclass. The two main forms are: 1. Compile-time (Static) Polymorphism: Achieved via method overloading or operator overloading where method signatures differ. 2. Runtime (Dynamic) Polymorphism: Achieved via method overriding where a subclass provides a specific implementation of a method already declared in its parent class.
3: Exception handling is a structured programming mechanism to handle unexpected runtime errors gracefully without crashing the entire application. It separates error handling code from normal business logic. Core components include: try block to enclose vulnerable code, catch/except block to catch and handle the specific error, and finally block to ensure cleanup routines (like closing file streams) always execute.
